title: moeb test_suite: event-driven end-to-end CLI command for full workflow validation including rubric escalation
description:
moeb has no integration test harness that exercises the full signal→fix_signal→spec→run→accept_candidate workflow against a known input. Consequences:

1. Regressions in any phase of the workflow are only discovered when real project signals fail — there is no synthetic baseline to detect breakage early.

2. moeb-source signals raised during client project runs (Ariadne accumulated 5 during two runs: a1000089, a1000090, a1000091, plus 2 duplicates of a1000056) prove that the workflow produces failures on real projects that would be caught by a minimal integration test.

3. The event emission contracts that Ouro relies on have never been end-to-end validated. A test suite that progresses via events rather than direct return values validates both the workflow logic and the event emission contract simultaneously. It acts as a minimal synchronous Ouro for test purposes.

4. Rubric escalation — moeb's self-healing mechanism that promotes signal-level rubric criteria to project-level rubrics for ongoing enforcement — has no automated verification path.

5. The 'awaiting_validation' lifecycle (signal a1000087) requires a lightweight signal→validate run primitive that is structurally identical to what the test suite exercises. The test suite provides the reference implementation for that primitive.
proposed_resolution:
Implement 'moeb test_suite' as a top-level CLI command. Full specification:

**Setup phase:**
1. Create a temporary isolated directory with a minimal Rust crate skeleton (Cargo.toml + src/lib.rs with a single stub function).
2. Run 'moeb init' in that directory. Assert the canonical .moeb structure is created: config.toml, signals/catalogue/, specifications/, rubrics/, events/, runs/.

**Known test signal:**
3. Write a fixed test signal to .moeb/signals/catalogue/: category NewCapability, title 'Add hello_world function', signal_source 'test_suite', description requiring 'pub fn hello_world() -> &str' returning a non-empty string. The signal must embed a rubric criterion in its description: 'any public function added by this change must have a doc comment'. This criterion must be escalated to .moeb/rubrics/ during the run as proof of the self-healing escalation mechanism. Signal must have a stable deterministic ID (e.g. test-signal-00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001) so the test suite can reference it without scanning.

**Event-driven state machine:**
The test suite drives each transition by invoking a moeb operation and then watching .moeb/events/ for the expected completion event. Each leg has a configurable per-leg timeout (flag --timeout-per-leg, default values in seconds: init=30, signal_created=60, fix_signal=60, spec=300, run=600, accept=120):

  [INIT]
    → moeb_init()
    → assert_init_structure()
  [SIGNAL_CREATED]
    → write_test_signal()
    → wait_for_event(SIGNAL_CREATED_EVENT, 60s)
  [FIX_SIGNAL]
    → invoke: moeb fix_signal --signal-id <test_signal_id>
    → wait_for_event(SIGNAL_SELECTED_EVENT, 60s)
  [SPEC_RUNNING]
    → wait_for_event(SPEC_COMPLETE_EVENT, 300s)
    → assert_spec_structure(): spec file exists at .moeb/specifications/, frontmatter contains signal_id matching test signal
  [RUN_RUNNING]
    → invoke: moeb run --signal-id <test_signal_id>  [requires a1000083]
    → wait_for_event(RUN_COMPLETE_EVENT, 600s)
    → assert_run_artifacts(): candidate tag exists, src/lib.rs modified, .moeb/rubrics/ contains escalated doc-comment criterion
  [ACCEPT]
    → invoke: moeb accept_candidate
    → wait_for_event(CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED_EVENT, 120s)
    → assert_accepted_state(): version bumped or accepted state recorded in run file

**Rubric escalation assertion (self-healing validation):**
After RUN_COMPLETE_EVENT, assert that .moeb/rubrics/ contains a criterion derived from the test signal's embedded rubric ('any public function added must have a doc comment'). If absent, report RUBRIC_ESCALATION_FAIL as a distinct failure class regardless of whether the implementation is otherwise correct. This validates the core moeb self-healing contract: a signal with a rubric requirement produces a permanent project-level rule.

**moeb signal failure reporting:**
After the final state (or on any timeout/failure), scan .moeb/signals/catalogue/ for any signals with signal_source 'moeb' created during the test run (compare first_seen timestamps against test start time). Each such signal is reported as a P0 failure in the test output with its title, severity, and description. The test suite exits non-zero if any moeb-source signal was raised. This makes the test suite self-referential: a clean moeb produces no signals when exercising its own workflow on a trivial input.

**Output:**
- Human-readable summary to stdout: phase-by-phase pass/fail, timing per leg, P0 signal list if any.
- Machine-readable JSON via --json flag: { phases: [{name, status, duration_ms, assertions: [...]}, ...], moeb_signals_raised: [...], overall: 'pass'|'fail'|'timeout' }.
- Exit code 0 = all assertions pass and no moeb signals raised. Exit code 1 = at least one assertion failed or moeb signal raised. Exit code 2 = timeout on any leg.

**CI integration note:**
The spec/run legs invoke LLM calls internally. For CI the command must support a --mock-llm flag that uses a deterministic stub (pre-canned spec + run output for the known test signal) so the structural assertions can be validated without live LLM cost. The live (no-flag) mode is the authoritative integration test.
